reviewContext.coreQuestion: Can the earner write a USDC number it did not really receive on-chain?
reviewContext.answer: YES — via the default first-run baseline=0 path (records pre-existing/seed balance as earned) and via the ungated production FOUNDER_DIR override (points wallet.json + baseline + ledger at attacker-controlled files). The earner CAN write a fabricated dollar.

evidence.description: FIND-001 confirmed fixed: FOUNDER_USDC_NOW seam is TEST-gated; prod uses TRUSTED_RPC
FIND-005 confirmed fixed: BASE_RPC_URL only honored under TEST; prod hardcodes mainnet.base.org

sprint1FixStatus.FIND-001-seam: FIXED (record-earn.mjs:53 TEST-gated; test case 6 proves prod ignores seam)
sprint1FixStatus.FIND-005-rpc: FIXED with caveat (record-earn.mjs:54 TEST-gated; residual single-RPC trust in TRUSTED_RPC)
sprint1FixStatus.FIND-003-wallet: PARTIAL — wallet read from wallet.json in prod, but wallet.json lives under the always-overridable FOUNDER_DIR (see FIND-008); positive binding anchors to a movable target
sprint1FixStatus.FIND-004-ledger: PARTIAL — allowlist startsWith(FOUNDER_DIR) holds for lexical traversal, but FOUNDER_DIR itself is attacker-controlled in prod so the anchor is circular (see FIND-008); symlinked state dir not resolved (path.resolve does not deref symlinks)
sprint1FixStatus.FIND-006-tests: PARTIAL — added prod-seam-ignored (case 6) and baseline-no-double-count (case 7) cases, but case 7 BLESSES the first-run pre-existing-balance fraud (see FIND-007); no FOUNDER_DIR-override, no real-RPC-failure, no symlink, no corrupt-baseline case
